spec.label: Lesson
spec.intent:
A lesson is the default full teaching resource. It introduces a concept,
builds understanding, models the method, gives students guided-to-independent
practice, and closes with a retention check.

A lesson teaches before it asks students to perform independently. It is not
a worksheet, not a quick reference, and not a quiz. The teacher should be
able to use it as the main classroom arc for first contact with a concept.

The pedagogical arc is: orient -> build -> model -> practice -> close.
Every section must serve that arc. The planner must not skip the modelling
step, and it must not turn the close into a second teaching section.

visuals.note: Visuals should support conceptual understanding, especially in orient and model. They are not decorative and should not displace the teaching arc.

optional.intent: An optional second build section is only justified when the concept has two distinct knowledge pieces that would overload a single section.
An optional extension practice section for deep lessons. Use only when students need a genuine second wave of application.

required.intent: Open the lesson and create felt need. Activate prior knowledge, set the context, and introduce the anchor example without fully teaching the concept yet.
Make the concept precise. Define vocabulary, state key facts, and name the central principle the lesson depends on.
Demonstrate the method on the anchor. Show the reasoning step by step before any independent work, and surface the main pitfall while the teacher is still guiding.
Move into independent application with a warm-to-cold progression that fits the inferred lesson mode and the lesson depth.
Consolidate the lesson, check retention, and bridge to what the concept enables next. Do not reteach the build section here.

validation: Must contain at least one practice-stack, short-answer, or fill-in-blank
Must contain a worked-example-card or process-steps in the model section
Must contain summary-block, quiz-check, or what-next-bridge in the close section
Must not use worked-example-card in the close section
At most two sections may require visuals

excluded.reflect: Reflection is not required at the close of every lesson.
excluded.evaluate: Extended evaluation needs explicit criteria and evidence space outside the first-exposure lesson slice.
excluded.transfer: Far transfer belongs after successful familiar application.
excluded.state-goal: The objective is already represented by lesson/section structure; do not spend a separate block repeating it.
excluded.investigate: Inquiry design requires a practical/investigation resource and its own evidence and page budget.
excluded.model-thinking: Deferred until decision-commentary generation can be evaluated reliably.

Resource type: Lesson

Resource intent:
A lesson is the default full teaching resource. It introduces a concept,
builds understanding, models the method, gives students guided-to-independent
practice, and closes with a retention check.

A lesson teaches before it asks students to perform independently. It is not

Depth: standard
Target time: 30-40 minutes
Section count: 5
Question count: 4-6
Depth note: This is the default lesson shape: orient, build, model, practice, close.


Resource sections and component rules:

Section role: orient
Intent: Open the lesson and create felt need. Activate prior knowledge, set the context, and introduce the anchor example without fully teaching the concept yet.
Preferred components: section-header, hook-hero, prerequisite-strip
Also allowed: explanation-block, callout-block, what-next-bridge, section-divider, diagram-block
Forbidden here: practice-stack, quiz-check, short-answer, fill-in-blank

Section role: build
Intent: Make the concept precise. Define vocabulary, state key facts, and name the central principle the lesson depends on.
Preferred components: definition-card, key-fact, explanation-block
Also allowed: definition-family, glossary-rail, insight-strip, comparison-grid, callout-block, diagram-block, diagram-compare
Forbidden here: practice-stack, quiz-check

Section role: model
Intent: Demonstrate the method on the anchor. Show the reasoning step by step before any independent work, and surface the main pitfall while the teacher is still guiding.
Preferred components: worked-example-card, process-steps
Also allowed: pitfall-alert, key-fact, callout-block, diagram-block, diagram-series

Section role: practice
Intent: Move into independent application with a warm-to-cold progression that fits the inferred lesson mode and the lesson depth.
Preferred components: practice-stack, reflection-prompt
Also allowed: quiz-check, student-textbox, short-answer, fill-in-blank, pitfall-alert, diagram-block

Section role: close
Intent: Consolidate the lesson, check retention, and bridge to what the concept enables next. Do not reteach the build section here.
Preferred components: summary-block, quiz-check, what-next-bridge
Also allowed: key-fact, reflection-prompt, callout-block
Forbidden here: worked-example-card

Validation rules:
- Must contain at least one practice-stack, short-answer, or fill-in-blank
- Must contain a worked-example-card or process-steps in the model section
- Must contain summary-block, quiz-check, or what-next-bridge in the close section
- Must not use worked-example-card in the close section
- At most two sections may require visuals

cards.title: Why Light is Essential
cards.objective: Explain why light is necessary for plants to make food

misconceptions.description: Plants can still make some food in the dark if they have water and carbon dioxide, because those are the ingredients.
Light's heat is what gives plants the energy to make food, so any warm source could work.
Only bright, direct sunlight can power photosynthesis; on cloudy days plants stop making food.

sections.title: Light as the Energy Source for Photosynthesis
sections.transition_note: Now that we have a concrete example, we'll look inside the leaf to see exactly why light is indispensable.

sections.title: With Light vs. Without Light: Seeing the Boundary
sections.transition_note: To be certain we understand the role of light, we'll compare what happens when light is present and when it is absent.

sections.title: Check Your Understanding
sections.transition_note: Now, let's check if you can distinguish the necessity of light from other common ideas.
